statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-19385 (PostgreSQL pg_dump heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code) affects PostgreSQL 16 releases before 16.15 and is fixed in PostgreSQL 16.15: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-19385/. The PostgreSQL 16.15 release notes list it: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.15/. Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD records it under its 16.15-r0 secfixes entry: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are published at 16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64, each built from the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version. We unpacked every one of these builds on both architectures. The affected program is pg_dump under /usr/libexec/postgresql16/ in the postgresql16-client package (pg_dumpall runs it), and the pg_dump version string (pg_dump (PostgreSQL) 16.x) in each build matches the package version, as does the banner of the server binary /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres. 16.15-r0, built from PostgreSQL 16.15, is the first published build carrying the fix. 16.13-r0 and 16.14-r0 are built from earlier PostgreSQL 16 releases and are affected.

CVE-2026-19385 (PostgreSQL pg_dump heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 17.11: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-19385/ lists 17.11 as the fixed release for major version 17, and the 17.11 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/, include it. Alpine's postgresql17 17.11-r0 is the upgrade to upstream 17.11 and lists CVE-2026-19385 under its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql17 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD at the aports revision for each package version (the current revision is linked above) and the upstream source release of the same version, and the postgres server binary in every published build (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, reports the matching PostgreSQL 17 release. pg_dump ships in the postgresql17-client package, and in every published build for Alpine 3.23, on both x86_64 and aarch64, it reports the same PostgreSQL 17 release as the package version. The earlier published builds for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0 and 17.10-r0) are built from earlier upstream releases and their server binaries report those older versions, and Alpine applies no backport of this fix to them, so they are recorded as affected; 17.11-r0 and later carry the fix.

CVE-2026-19385 (PostgreSQL pg_dump heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 18.6: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-19385/ lists 18.6 as the fixed release for major version 18. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/3392cce5c92ea4c84b8a5088b4717066fd280056 ('pg_dump: avoid assuming how long pg_proc.protrftypes can be') on the REL_18_STABLE branch. Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-19385 under its 18.5-r0 secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built with that APKBUILD from the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version. We checked every postgresql18 build published for Alpine 3.23 as of 2026-11-27 (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64. In each, the postgres server reports the PostgreSQL release matching the package version. The message the fix adds to pg_dump, 'could not parse numeric array "%s": too few numbers', is in /usr/libexec/postgresql18/pg_dump (postgresql18-client package) of 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 and absent from 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0 and 18.4-r0 (the neighbouring 'too many numbers' message is older and is in every build, so it is not a marker). This owner has no 18.5-r0 build. 18.6-r0 is the first published build for Alpine 3.23 carrying the fix; 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0 and 18.4-r0 are affected.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-19385, a heap buffer overflow in pg_dump of long function transform lists that lets an object creator execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running pg_dump, in 17.11. Within major version 17, releases before 17.11 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-19385/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.11-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6438-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-19385. The fixed version is this owner's first rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1, which packages PostgreSQL 17.11 and is no longer in the repository. Every build published now carries the fix: the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.11 in the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 and in the 17.11-1 build, and PostgreSQL 17.12 in the 17.12-0 build and in the rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1, on amd64 and arm64. The earlier rebuild of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, packages PostgreSQL 17.10; it is affected and sorts below the fixed version.
